Protocol model

Front is the regional account and session connection. It uses protobuf RPC over WebSocket. Sunken is the native SC2 service connection. It uses schema-delimited, bit-packed records over TCP.

Front

Regional Battle.net login and session setup.

Message boundary: One WebSocket binary message.

→

Sunken

Native SC2 services over a separate TCP connection.

Record boundary: A service schema or the fixed command-response layout sets the boundary.

Message formats

Read each diagram from left to right. Each size is a wire size. A dashed edge identifies a conditional field or a schema-sized field.

Front
  1. The 2-byte prefix gives the RPC header size. Its value equals the number of protobuf-header bytes.
  2. The WebSocket message sets the frame boundary. The body ends with the WebSocket binary message.
  3. The header routes the call. The service and method select the operation. The token identifies the related request.
  4. Header.size is optional. If this field is present, its value must equal the body size.

Parser sketchread_u16_be → decode Header → decode body from remaining WebSocket bytes

Sunken

The route, payload, and padding share one continuous bit cursor. The worked example below shows how those parts occupy actual bytes.

Command responses
the one record shape with no payload

A record whose service flag is zero has a fixed two-byte form: six command bits, the zero service flag, and a nine-bit result. It has no service slot or typed payload.

Command-response boundary6 command + 1 service flag + 9 result = 16 bits

Connection sequence

Front identifies the account and selects an SC2 game account. Sunken proves possession of the Front authorization. Blizzard calls this process Resume.

Protocol reference

Front

Connection

Front RPC

Front carries Battle.net protobuf RPC before SC2 starts the Sunken service stream. The client contains protobuf descriptors for the services used here.

RPC framing

The Base97563 client first opens TLS to the regional Front endpoint. The client then performs an RFC 6455 upgrade. The WebSocket subprotocol is v1.rpc.battle.net. One binary WebSocket message contains one Front RPC message.

The server must select the same WebSocket subprotocol. A different or missing selection is rejected.

offset  size                 description
------  -------------------  ----------------------------------------------
0       2                    header length, unsigned big-endian
2       header_length        protobuf bgs.protocol.Header
...     remainder of message protobuf request/response body

uint16_be header_length
bytes     header[header_length]
bytes     body[websocket_message_end - current_offset]

The WebSocket message sets the frame boundary. Header.size validates the body byte count when present.

The WebSocket library applies RFC 6455 client masking. The Front decoder receives the unmasked binary-message payload. Server messages arrive unmasked.

An empty or truncated Front header is rejected. WebSocket messages are limited to 16 MiB.

Header fieldProtobuf wire typeMeaning
1 service_idvarintNumeric dispatch value. The first Connect uses 0. Responses use 0xfe.
2 method_idvarintMethod number within the selected service.
3 tokenvarintRequest/callback correlation token.
4 object_idvarintOptional addressed service object.
5 sizevarintBody byte count.
6 statusvarintRPC result/status code.
7 errorlength-delimited, repeatedStructured error details.
8 timeoutvarintOptional request timeout.
9 is_responsevarint booleanExplicit response marker when present.
10 forward_targetslength-delimited, repeatedOptional process forwarding targets.
11 service_hashfixed32FNV-1a hash of the full protobuf service name. Protobuf fixed32 is little-endian on the wire.
13 client_idlength-delimited UTF-8Optional client identifier.
14 fanout_targetlength-delimited, repeatedOptional structured fanout targets.
15 client_id_fanout_targetlength-delimited UTF-8, repeatedOptional client-ID fanout targets.
16 client_recordlength-delimited bytesOptional opaque client record.

Dispatch and callbacks

The service and method fields select the operation. The token identifies the related call. These functions are independent.

Each request sets service_id=0 and uses the 32-bit FNV-1a hash of the full protobuf service name. This rule includes the first Connect request.

h = 0x811c9dc5
for each UTF-8 byte b in full_service_name:
    h = h XOR b
    h = (h * 0x01000193) AND 0xffffffff

Relevant names include:

  • bnet.protocol.connection.ConnectionService
  • bnet.protocol.authentication.AuthenticationServer
  • bnet.protocol.authentication.AuthenticationClient
  • bnet.protocol.challenge.ChallengeNotify
  • bnet.protocol.game_utilities.GameUtilities
  • bnet.protocol.account.AccountService
  • bnet.protocol.session.SessionService and SessionListener

A server-to-client call uses a listener service. If the descriptor declares a response, the client must send a response. Set service_id to 0xfe. Copy the callback token. Set the status to zero.

If the return type is NO_RESPONSE, the client omits the response frame. An empty declared response still requires a response frame.

The authentication loop dispatches callbacks while its request tokens are pending. Outside that loop, only ConnectionService.Echo is handled automatically. Any other unexpected callback is rejected.

Logon sequence

StepDirectionService / methodNotes
1C→SConnectionService / 1Use service_id=0, token=0, and the ConnectionService hash. Advertise bindless RPC.
2C→SAuthenticationServer / 1Send program S2, platform Mc64, locale enUS, the embedded SDK identity, and application_version=0. A cached credential is optional.
3S→CChallengeNotify / 3Send an external web_auth_url challenge when necessary. The method is NO_RESPONSE.
4local HTTPSBattle.net account flowWhen challenged, cookies, MFA, CAPTCHA, and account state stay in the web view.
5C→SAuthenticationServer / 7Submit the short-lived credential from the web flow.
6S→CAuthenticationClient / 5LogonResult: account, game accounts, region, and 64-byte session key.
7C→SAuthenticationServer / 8Generate a new cached credential. Replace the accepted cached credential.
8C→SGameUtilities / 1Start the SC2 Front bootstrap directly after authentication.

For Base97563, LogonRequest.version contains this exact embedded SDK identity:

Battle.net Game Service SDK v1.48.2 "cf68e241e0"/104 (Jul 14 2026 19:45:54)

Protobuf field 6, application_version, is zero. Use the embedded SDK identity and this fixed field value independently of the installation build number.

Authentication callbacks can occur between RPC responses. Method 10 reports a logon update. Method 14 reports game-account selection. Methods 11 through 13 are NO_RESPONSE. The client must dispatch these methods as callbacks.

The web view handles only the account challenge. The Front connection remains the protocol client. The client submits the short-lived credential with AuthenticationServer method 7.

The cached credential from method 8 and the short-lived challenge credential are separate values. A cached credential can prevent the next web challenge. Replace it after successful use. If the server rejects it, start the web challenge.

Sunken session request

The client sends GameUtilities.ProcessClientRequest method 1. The ClientRequest contains only the required fields. Top-level field 1 contains typed attributes. Top-level field 4 contains the first SC2 game-account entity from LogonResult.

The later game-account selection callback is validated. The request continues to use the first entity from LogonResult.

The request omits the host-process, Battle.net-account, program, and client-info fields.

Attribute nameVariant typeCurrent value shape
LogonTokenRequeststring"0.0.1"
environmentstringRegional environment string; "US" for this target.
session_keyblob64 private bytes from LogonResult.
localestring"enUS"

An Attribute contains protobuf field 1, name. It also contains protobuf field 2, Variant. The following field numbers select the Variant type:

  • 2: Boolean
  • 3: signed integer
  • 4: double
  • 5: string
  • 6: blob
  • 7: embedded message
  • 8: FourCC string
  • 9: unsigned integer
  • 10: entity ID

A successful response contains another attribute set. The handoff requires these attributes:

  • address: native endpoint string;
  • session_key: exactly 64 private bytes;
  • account_region: unsigned integer in 0..255;
  • game_account_name and account_mail: private identity strings;
  • logon_response: a bit-packed native LogonResponse3.

These attributes transfer the session from Front to Sunken. The handoff section defines their use.

RPC envelope

message Header {
  required uint32  service_id              = 1;
  optional uint32  method_id               = 2;
  required uint32  token                   = 3;
  optional uint64  object_id               = 4 [default = 0];
  optional uint32  size                    = 5 [default = 0];
  optional uint32  status                  = 6 [default = 0];
  repeated ErrorInfo error                   = 7;

  repeated ProcessId forward_targets        = 10;
  optional fixed32 service_hash            = 11;
  optional string  client_id               = 13;
  repeated FanoutTarget fanout_target          = 14;
  repeated string  client_id_fanout_target = 15;
  optional bytes   client_record           = 16;
}

Sunken session

Starting Sunken

Front authenticates the Battle.net account and selects an SC2 game account. It then supplies the data for the Sunken connection.

The logon_response attribute contains a bit-packed Battlenet::Client::Authentication::LogonResponse3. This type contains the status, authentication requests, timeouts, regulator rules, account data, and optional RAF state.

The selected BSN metadata type determines the protobuf blob's logical bit length. All unused bits in the last byte must be zero.

The address attribute contains the Sunken host and optional port. Port 1119 is used when the string omits it. A bracketed IPv6 address can include a port after the closing bracket.

The client can open the Sunken TCP connection before Front closes. The client must send Auth/1 ResumeRequest after Front closes. Front and Sunken are independent TCP connections.

The Front protocol defines RequestDisconnect method 7 and ForceDisconnect method 4. The documented handoff sends a WebSocket close frame directly.

The Sunken TCP connection opens first, followed by the Front close. Auth/1 ResumeRequest is sent after the close call succeeds.

After the handoff, the client uses the Sunken transport and payload format. The Sunken record section defines its bit cursor, header, and boundary.

Back to overview

Sunken

Record format

Sunken record stream

A Sunken service record begins with an 11-bit route. That route selects the payload schema whose fields determine where the record ends.

The complete Chat/2 Sunken record shows the route, payload, padding, and boundary in two actual bytes.

Routing header

The first seven bits identify the command and distinguish service records from command responses. A service record then reads a four-bit service slot.

record ServiceRoute {
    command_id: u6,
    service_present: u1 = 1,
    service_slot: u4,
}

For a service record, the payload starts at bit 3 of the second byte.

for a route with a service slot
byte0 = (command & 0x3f) | 0x40 | (((slot >> 3) & 1) << 7)
byte1 bits 0..2 = slot & 0x07

Bit order

The decoder keeps one (byte index, bit index) cursor for the entire record. Within each byte, it consumes bit 0 first and bit 7 last. After bit 7, the cursor continues at bit 0 of the next byte.

A multi-bit value can cross that boundary. The first chunk becomes the higher-order part of the result, as the split four-bit service slot does in the walkthrough.

read(width):
    value = 0
    while width remains:
        take = min(width, bits_left_in_current_byte)
        chunk = (current_byte >> current_bit_offset) & ((1 << take) - 1)
        value = (value << take) | chunk
        advance(take)

Command response

When service_present is zero, the record is decoded as a fixed command response with a nine-bit result.

record CommandResponse {
    command_id: u6,
    service_present: u1 = 0,
    result: u9,
}

The command response consists of the command, service flag, and result. These fields total 16 bits and end on a byte boundary.

Record boundaries

A service record carries no total byte count. Its route selects a top-level type. Decoding that type advances the cursor to the logical end. Zero padding then advances the cursor to the next byte boundary.

How a selected schema determines its own extent.
Schema formBits consumed
Fixed-width valueThe width stored in BSN metadata.
Array, string, or blobA local bounded count followed by that many elements or bytes.
Optional valueA presence bit followed by the nested value when present.
ChoiceA bounded selector followed by the selected arm.
StructureEvery member in its wire layout, including filler runs.

A count uses the bounded-integer encoding. For a range [minimum..maximum], metadata gives the bit width. The wire stores value - minimum. For example, [1..64] stores count - 1 in six bits. A fixed range consumes zero count bits.

The general calculation is:

logical_bits = routing_header_bits + payload_bits_consumed_by_schema
padding_bits = (-logical_bits) & 7
record_bytes = (logical_bits + padding_bits) / 8

An incremental decoder applies the selected schema directly to buffered bytes. If a field is incomplete, the decoder reads more TCP data. After the schema ends, it validates zero padding. The next routing header starts at the next byte.

Parsing

  1. Read the six-bit command and one-bit service flag.
  2. For a command response, read its nine-bit result and finish the two-byte record.
  3. For a service record, read the four-bit slot.
  4. Resolve (direction, slot, command) to a top-level type.
  5. Decode that type, applying a generated wire layout where one exists.
  6. Require zero bits through the next byte boundary. The following byte begins the next record.
Unknown service routes. The payload schema is normally necessary to calculate the boundary. The current parser skips Prty/0 as 18 bytes and slot 13 command 50 as 38 bytes. Any other unknown route stops decoding.

Internal alignment applies to the complete record. A string, byte string, or blob can align the cursor before its raw bytes. Encode the route and payload with one cursor beginning at bit zero of the complete record.

The static service map assigns each implemented slot. The metadata section defines the selected payload type.

BSN metadata

Embedded BSN schema metadata

A Sunken service route selects the payload schema. The payload schema sets the service-record boundary. A service-less command response uses its fixed 16-bit layout.

SC2 embeds compact version-7 BSN metadata in the client executable. Source-path strings in the documented client identify the producer as bsnc version 2.2.13.

bsnc is Blizzard's schema compiler and serialization runtime for Sunken's bit-packed protocol. It turns protocol definitions into native encoders, decoders, size calculators, and compact metadata tables. Those tables describe type kinds, member references, names, integer and count widths, accepted ranges, and control flags. Generated readers, writers, and layout sidecars supply field permutations and filler runs for selected types.

A normal client can use a generated static schema. Inspection tools can load a metadata file or extract the largest metadata block from an executable.

Schema lookup

Each metadata type has a build-specific numeric ID. The ID selects a structural record. It can also select a naming record. A structural record can refer to other type IDs. Thus, one payload type produces a type graph.

The definitions in this document summarize the decoded type graph. They show values and relationships. Separate wire-layout data supplies generated field order and filler runs.

The metadata block contains a dump-offset table and a name-offset table. A type ID is the zero-based position used to read both tables. For the documented client build, type ID 351 selects the structural record and name record for Battlenet::Authentication::ModuleRequest.

The decoded definition of that record is an array whose count occupies three bits, whose accepted range is 0..=4, and whose element type resolves to ModuleInput. Authentication::ProofRequest reaches it through the following metadata entries:

TypeDeclaration
ProofRequest (record 1422) Member m_request resolves through alias 1424 to type 351.
ModuleRequest (record 351) Kind array; 3-bit count; accepted range 0..=4; element alias 352 resolves to record 346.
ModuleInput (record 346) Struct containing m_id and m_data.
ModuleId (record 344) Alias resolving to a fixed 40-byte blob.
ModuleData (record 345) Kind blob; 10-bit byte count; accepted range 0..=1023.

These IDs remain in the decoder's schema lookup. Applying the resolved types produces this Sunken record layout:

record AuthProofRequest {
    command_id: u6 = 2,
    service_present: u1 = 1,
    service_slot: u4 = 0,
    payload: ProofRequest,
    final_alignment: byte,
}

struct ProofRequest {
    requests: ModuleRequest,
}

type ModuleRequest = Array<ModuleInput> {
    count_bits: 3,
    count_range: 0..=4,
}

struct ModuleInput {
    id: ModuleId,
    data: ModuleData,
}

type ModuleData = Blob {
    byte_count_bits: 10,
    byte_count_range: 0..=1023,
    alignment: byte,
}

requests is the logical field represented by request_count and the repeated values. Three bits can represent 0..=7; the declared range rejects 5..=7.

Type kinds

The low six bits of a structural record identify one of 16 kinds. The kind defines the remaining metadata. The kind also defines how the value consumes the Sunken bitstream.

Scalar values

5 Boolean
One bit.
7 enum
A bounded integer, optionally restricted to listed values.
8 FourCC
Exactly 32 bits.
9 integer
A bounded, fixed-width integer.
10 void
Zero bits.
12 float32
32 raw bits.
13 float64
64 raw bits.

Containers

1 array
Metadata-sized element count, then that many values of another type.
2 byte string
Metadata-sized byte count, byte alignment, then that many raw bytes.
3 bit array
Metadata-sized bit count, then that many packed bits.
4 blob
Metadata-sized byte count, byte alignment, then that many raw bytes.
11 optional
One presence bit, then the contained value when present.
15 UTF-8 string
Metadata-sized byte count, alignment, then that many UTF-8 bytes.

Composition

6 choice
A bounded selector followed by the selected arm.
14 struct
A sequence of named or unnamed member types.
16 alias
A transparent reference to another type.

Most bounded values encode value - minimum. Metadata supplies the bit width. A fixed-size value can omit the count. For some indexed types, bit 7 identifies a continuous index range.

Metadata storage

Use this binary layout to extract BSN metadata from an SC2 build. Network records contain values selected by the extracted schemas.

Header5 × big-endian u32
→
Shape offsetsone u32 per type ID
→
Shape recordsdump_size bytes
→
Name offsetsone u32 per type ID
→
Name recordsstring_size bytes

Type ID n selects element n in both offset tables. The shape offset points to the structural record. The name offset points to a naming record. A zero name offset identifies an unnamed type.

The naming record contains 32-bit offsets into a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string pool. The type_count, dump_size, and string_size fields set the five region boundaries.

struct MetadataHeader {
    version: BeU32, // currently 7
    flags: BeU32,
    type_count: BeU32,
    dump_size: BeU32,
    string_size: BeU32,
}

struct MetadataBlock {
    header: MetadataHeader,
    dump_offsets: Array<BeU32>, // length = type_count
    dump_data: Blob {
        alignment: byte,
    },
    string_record_offsets: Array<BeU32>, // length = type_count
    string_data: Blob {
        alignment: byte,
    },
}

The first byte of each structural record begins with:

bits 0..5  kind tag (1..16)
bit  6     generated-handling marker
bit  7     kind-specific compact-form flag

The selected kind defines bit 7. For example, bit 7 can identify an implicit continuous index range.

Generated wire layouts

Sunken metadata provides logical field names, types, and constraints. SC2's generated codecs can transmit a structure in a different field order and insert filler bits between fields.

Layout storage

The SC2 5.0.16.97563 client contains two forms of layout data:

  • A generic runtime table. Obfuscator::GetStruct(type_id) returns a pointer to a field count followed by packed u32 entries.
  • Generated per-type code. Many readers, writers, and size functions have the field sequence and filler calls compiled directly into their instructions.

The complete mapping is distributed across that runtime table and the generated functions. The embedded metadata supplies the authoritative list of marked types. Generated reader, writer, and size behavior supplies the authoritative layout for each marked type.

The 0x40 marker

Bit 6 of a metadata type tag is stored as the Obfuscated flag. Its effect is mechanical:

  1. The metadata parser keeps the flag alongside the low six-bit type kind.
  2. A generic encoder created without an Obfuscator checks the flag. A marked type triggers a safety assertion unless reflection fallback was enabled.
  3. With an Obfuscator, a non-null entry supplies field order and filler widths.
  4. The decoder follows a supplied entry. A null entry uses metadata field order.

The bit carries no field indices or filler widths. A decoder needs the separate per-type entry, the generated reader, or verified metadata-order behavior.

Table format

A structure entry begins with its reflected field count. One packed u32 follows for each field, in transmitted order. Bits 0 through 25 select the logical field. Bits 26 through 31 give the filler width immediately before that field.

struct WireField {
    logical_field: u32, // entry & 0x03ff_ffff
    filler_before: u6, // entry >> 26
}

struct StructWireLayout {
    field_count: u64,
    fields: Array<WireField> { count: field_count },
}
for entry in layout.fields {
    reader.skip(entry.filler_before);
    values[entry.logical_field] = decode(logical_fields[entry.logical_field]);
}

Filler bits

SC2 derives filler from a rolling u32 state seeded with the structure's field count. Before each filler run, the writer mixes the current bit position and preceding output bytes into that state, rotates it left by eight, and writes the requested low bits. Reproducing SC2's output requires this algorithm.

The client decoder advances over each run without reading its value. Server-side validation of filler values has not been observed.

Example: Club::InviteAction

Metadata lists club_id, member, code, and result. The generated client codec sends this sequence:

struct InviteActionWire {
    code: InviteCode,
    member: ToonHandle,
    club_id: ClubId,
    filler: u11,
    result: ErrorCode,
}

The corresponding packed entries are:

const INVITE_ACTION_LAYOUT: Array<WireField> = [
    WireField { logical_field: 2, filler_before: 0 },
    WireField { logical_field: 1, filler_before: 0 },
    WireField { logical_field: 0, filler_before: 0 },
    WireField { logical_field: 3, filler_before: 11 },
];

Resume

Sunken Resume

Resume starts after the Front handoff. Sunken waits for the client to send Auth/1 as the first record.

Resume

Resume is a Blizzard type name. The BSN metadata contains the types Battlenet::Client::Authentication::ResumeRequest and Battlenet::Client::Authentication::ResumeResponse. Client-to-server Auth/1 selects ResumeRequest. Server-to-client Auth/1 selects ResumeResponse.

Resume continues the authenticated session context. Front authenticates the Battle.net account. Front selects the SC2 game account. GameUtilities returns the Sunken endpoint and the session data. Resume proves possession of this data on the new connection.

Native authentication entry points named in the embedded metadata
RouteEmbedded request typeStarting context
Auth/0LogonRequest3Cold native account logon; asks the native service to choose account-logon modules.
Auth/1ResumeRequestContinues the account and game-account session authorized by the Front handoff. This is the path documented here.
Auth/17SingleSignOnRequest3Begins from a native SSO identifier supplied by another trusted context.

Auth/1 ResumeRequest

Logical payload definition:

struct ResumeRequest {
    common: RequestCommon,
    account: Blob {
        alignment: byte,
    },
    game_account_region: u8, // from Front LogonResponse3
    game_account_name: Blob {
        alignment: byte,
    },
}

struct RequestCommon {
    program: FourCC, // "S2"
    platform: FourCC, // "Mc64"
    locale: FourCC, // "enUS"
    versions: [Version; 5], // values in the table below
}
ProgramComponent/platformVersion
S2NGD10x5bc8dcc1
S2NGD20xfade3a32
S2NGD30x0c129365
S2NGD40x86b7c0ed
BnetMc640x000a16a7 (661159)

These values apply to Base97563. The native compatibility number is an independent protocol constant. The Front LogonRequest separately sends application_version=0.

The client must send all four S2/NGD* records followed by the exact Bnet/Mc64 record shown above.

Proof exchange

The Resume ProofRequest contains two 40-byte module IDs. Each ID contains an eight-byte usage prefix and a 32-byte module identity.

  1. Thumbprint module. The server sends a 4096-bit RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 SHA-512 signature. Hash the 16-byte peer address and then the ASCII domain Thumbprint.IPv6. Convert an IPv4 address to IPv4-mapped IPv6. Verify the signature with exponent 65537 and the SC2 public modulus. The wire signature is little-endian. Reverse its 512 bytes before RSA verification. Verification occurs locally and yields zero ModuleOutput elements.
  2. Session-proof module. The server data is 00 || server_nonce[16]. Use the 64-byte GameUtilities value as seed B. Generate client_nonce[16]. Calculate key C with the formula below. Send 01 || client_nonce || HMAC-SHA256(C, 00 || client_nonce || server_nonce). Verify the proof in the successful ResumeResponse.

For GameUtilities seed B, client nonce Nc, and server nonce Ns, the Resume ratchet and proofs are:

C = HMAC-SHA256(B, 0x00 || Nc || Ns)
 || HMAC-SHA256(B, 0x01 || Ns || Nc)

client_proof    = HMAC-SHA256(C, 0x00 || Nc || Ns)
server_proof    = HMAC-SHA256(C, 0x01 || Ns || Nc)
transport_secret = C

Resume first converts seed B to C. Auth/2 proofs and transport-key derivation use C. The domain-two KDF belongs to the full-logon handshake.

An optional plaintext Conn/11 RegulatorUpdate can appear before Auth/1 ResumeResponse.

Stream protection

The client must validate the server proof. The client then sends an empty Conn/5 EnableEncryption record in plaintext. Both directions then use stateful RC4 beginning with the first keystream byte.

inbound_key  = HMAC-SHA256(transport_secret,
                68e0c72eddd6d2f31e5ab155b18b631e)
outbound_key = HMAC-SHA256(transport_secret,
                dea965ae543a1e939e690caa68de7839)

The inbound and outbound RC4 states are independent. Each state continues across TCP operations and Sunken record boundaries, independent of TCP segmentation.

One receive operation can contain a plaintext ResumeResponse and protected bytes. In this case, enable the inbound state after ResumeResponse. Decrypt the protected suffix one time.

After protection starts, the connection starts the native service bootstrap.

Back to overview

Identity

Identity and presence

The protocol uses several identifier namespaces for the same person. Account and character identities are stable. Presence IDs and member handles belong to one native connection or joined channel.

Identity path

  1. Front logon returns a Battle.net account entity ID and one or more game-account entity IDs. These are 128-bit protobuf entity values.
  2. The selected SC2 game account is passed to Game Utilities. Its response supplies the native game-account name, region, session key, and native logon response used by Resume.
  3. After Resume, Toon/0 lists the playable SC2 identities owned by that game account. Toon/5 selects one; Toon/6 returns its stable ToonHandle and profile record address.
  4. Pres/0 associates that stable identity and native account data with connection-local presence IDs.
  5. Chat/1 associates a channel-local member handle with a presence ID. The chain can then resolve a message sender to account, toon, profile, and display state.

Identifier namespaces

IdentifierScopeMeaningRelated namespace
Front account EntityIdBattle.net accountThe platform account returned by Front logon.Native 32-bit account ID.
Front game-account EntityIdOne game license/accountThe selected SC2 game account passed to Game Utilities.Battle.net account entity or toon.
Native game-account nameResume sessionThe SC2 game-account string returned by Game Utilities.A toon display name.
Native account_idSocial servicesA 32-bit Battle.net account key used by Presence, Friends, Profile, and whisper targets.Either Front protobuf entity ID.
ToonFullNameName-based SC2 identityRegion, program, realm, and display name. Prfl/3 resolves it to a handle.A stable handle.
ToonHandleStable SC2 characterRegion, program, realm, and 64-bit toon ID.Profile address or account ID.
RecordAddressProfile storageA label and 64-bit record ID used by Prfl/0.Toon handle.
Local/master presence IDOne native connectionAliases for an online presence record announced by Pres/0.Stable account or toon identity.
Channel indexOne connectionA three-bit slot assigned to one joined channel.Public channel name ID.
Member handleOne joined channelA roster member key used by Chat messages and membership changes.Presence ID or account ID.

Identity cardinality

One Battle.net account can own multiple game accounts. One SC2 game account can expose region- and realm-specific toons. One stable account or toon can appear through more than one presence alias, and the same presence can participate in several channels under a different member handle in each channel.

Use a native account ID or toon handle as the durable person key. Merge local and master presence IDs announced together. When two presence records expose the same nonzero native account ID, fold them to the same social identity while retaining every connection-local alias needed for routing.

Presence links

Pres/1 first defines field handles and widths. A later Pres/0 value can then carry the links below:

FieldValueRelationship
0x00010005native account IDPrimary stable social-account link.
0x0001001bnative account IDSecondary social-account link.
65561ToonHandleStable SC2 character link.
65556RecordAddressProfile data and avatar lookup link.
65555ImageTableEntryDirect avatar link when present.

Pres/4 starts with a stable ToonHandle and asks the server to create temporary presence. Its immediate response reports only a result. A later Pres/0 supplies the connection-local presence ID. That ID can then be used by the LocalPresenceId whisper target.

Channel members

struct MembershipChangeJoining {
    member_handle: u32, // local to one joined channel
    presence_id: u32, // local to the native connection
    statuses: Array<MemberStatus>,
}

An incoming Chat/11 message names only the channel index and member handle. Resolve the member handle through the roster, then resolve its presence ID through the Presence store. Only after those two local lookups is it safe to associate the message with a native account ID, toon handle, profile address, display name, avatar, or standing state.

Profiles and friends

Prfl/1 maps a native account ID to a profile record address. Prfl/3 maps a ToonFullName to a stable ToonHandle. Frnd/6 carries the inverse social links in bulk: native account ID, full toon name, and profile address. These mappings join identity namespaces while preserving the scope of each numeric value.

Back to overview

Services

Sunken service routing

The routing header contains a four-bit service slot. Thus, one build can use at most 16 slot values. Each record carries the numeric slot, and build-specific constants assign readable service names.

The wire route is (direction, slot, command). The implementation keeps separate inbound and outbound code paths. Its inbound table looks up (slot, command). Service names such as Chat are readable labels for the static slot values.

Service slots

The table matches the build-specific constants and dispatch tables. The directions show records that can currently be encoded or decoded.

The table lists service records. Inbound command responses set the service flag to zero and use the fixed 16-bit layout.

SlotLabelClient → serverServer → client
0Auth0, 1, 2, 16, 170, 1, 2, 16, 18
1Conn5, 10, 12, 131, 3, 11, 13, 14
3Frnd66, 30, 31, 33
4Pres0, 2, 40, 1, 3, 4
5Chat0, 2, 5, 6, 9, 11, 19, 21, 23, 25, 321, 4, 11, 13, 19, 22, 24, 26, 27, 30, 33

11Cach99

Chat/20 awaits an inbound type mapping. The stream has boundary-only skips for Prty/0 and slot 13 command 50.

The route dispatch table combines the slot and command to select a top-level type. The metadata section defines its recursive schema.

Back to overview

Sunken service endpoints

Sunken uses service command endpoints addressed by (direction, slot, command). A static build table assigns the FourCC-like service labels.

Payload notation

Each block describes the route and its payload in wire order. Named types link to their entries in the Sunken type registry.

struct Namefields appear in the displayed order
type Name = Array<T> { … }a count prefix followed by that many values
type Name = Blob { … }a byte count followed by that many bytes
Optional<T> { presence_bits: 1 }a presence bit followed by T when set
uNan unsigned field consumes exactly N bits, such as u1 or u6
Reserved<N>N generated filler or reserved bits
Bytes<N>exactly N byte-aligned bytes
alignment: byteadvance to the next byte boundary after the value

count_bits and byte_count_bits give the width of the transmitted count. The corresponding count_range states the values accepted by the metadata. Field names use snake case and omit the leading m_ prefix.

Generated order means the struct follows the wire. Logical order means the struct follows metadata and requires a generated-order note.

  • Auth authentication
  • Conn connection
  • Achv achievements
  • Toon identity
  • Pres presence
  • Frnd friends
  • Cach cache streams
  • S2Ms master data
  • Prty party state
  • S2Mp multiplayer
  • Prfl profile
  • Chat channels

The entries follow Resume and post-logon traffic. A generated order includes reserved bits that the serializer adds. An incomplete entry identifies the unknown part.

Auth/2 Authentication::ProofRequest

Direction
server → client
Phase
plaintext
Structure
logical order
Evidence
verified

Requests execution of up to four authentication modules. The array count occupies three bits and has the accepted range 0..=4. Resume encodes count 2 for the thumbprint and session-proof modules.

record AuthProofRequest {
    command_id: u6 = 2,
    service_present: u1 = 1,
    service_slot: u4 = 0,
    payload: ProofRequest,
    final_alignment: byte,
}

struct ProofRequest {
    requests: ModuleRequest,
}

type ModuleRequest = Array<ModuleInput> {
    count_bits: 3,
    count_range: 0..=4,
}

struct ModuleInput {
    id: ModuleId,
    data: ModuleData,
}

type ModuleData = Blob {
    byte_count_bits: 10,
    byte_count_range: 0..=1023,
    alignment: byte,
}

The 40-byte module identifier selects the authentication-module implementation that must interpret data. The Sunken routing header carries the separate six-bit Auth/2 command ID.

struct ModuleId {
    usage: Bytes<8>, // b"auth\0\0\0\0"
    identity: Bytes<32>,
}

const THUMBPRINT_ID: Bytes<32> = [
    0xd7, 0xe6, 0x62, 0x40, 0x80, 0xc1, 0xab, 0xa6,
    0x6d, 0xee, 0x63, 0xa6, 0xf3, 0x92, 0x8d, 0x8a,
    0x54, 0x69, 0x25, 0x7f, 0x58, 0x20, 0xb5, 0x72,
    0x1f, 0xb8, 0xc3, 0x2b, 0x6b, 0x5b, 0xef, 0x5d,
];

const SESSION_PROOF_ID: Bytes<32> = [
    0x89, 0x50, 0x05, 0x34, 0x0a, 0x63, 0x0a, 0x64,
    0x65, 0xa6, 0x5f, 0xec, 0x96, 0x32, 0x3c, 0x31,
    0x0b, 0xca, 0x8a, 0x9f, 0x66, 0xec, 0xee, 0xb1,
    0x88, 0x7a, 0x9d, 0x6c, 0x0e, 0x67, 0x61, 0x2e,
];

Resume supplies these two modules in the order shown. The explicit three-bit count supplies their cardinality; the native schema delimits the complete record.

Direction
client → server
Phase
plaintext
Structure
logical order
Evidence
verified

Returns outputs requested by the authentication modules. The thumbprint module is verified locally and emits zero outputs. The Resume response therefore contains one session-proof output.

struct ProofResponse {
    responses: Array<ModuleOutput> {
        count_bits: 3,
        count_range: 0..=4,

    data: Blob {
        byte_count_bits: 10,
        byte_count_range: 0..=1023,
        alignment: byte,
    },
}

The session-proof output is 01 || client_nonce[16] || proof[32], for a byte count of 49.

Reflection lists frame type and headers before the payload. Using that order corrupts the following record.

Retail sends two maintenance requests to TrnC one time each minute. Command 3 contains four zero bytes. Command 2 contains 030080057e4002020a0301. Both requests are CS_ROUTED frames. Their correlation headers set reply = false. A retail-compatible client must send these requests and Conn/10 Ping.

Pres/0 Presence::UpdateNotify

Direction
server → client
Phase
protected
Structure
generated order
Evidence
verified

Updates online state and announced fields. Read field data in handle order. Use the fixed size from Pres/1 or the next variable size. A cleared handle removes its stored value. Local and master presence IDs identify the same stored record.

struct UpdateNotify {
    _reserved_0: Reserved<19>,
    online: bool,
    local_presence_id: u32,
    master_presence_id: u32,
    field_data: Blob {
        byte_count_bits: 11,
        byte_count_range: 0..=1024,
        alignment: byte,
    },
    _reserved_1: Reserved<11>,
    cleared_handles: Array<u32> {
        count_bits: 4,
    },
    handles: Array<u32> {
        count_bits: 4,
    },
    variable_sizes: Array<u16> {
        count_bits: 4,
    },
    level_zero: Optional<LevelZero>,
    server_only: u8,
}

struct LevelZero {
    is_last_packet: bool,
    target: u32,
}

FIELD_AVATAR (65555) is a four-byte ImageTableEntry. Public channel membership usually supplies FIELD_TOON_PROFILE (65556); its 12-byte profile address is followed through Prfl/0 path 04 to obtain the selected avatar.

The client reads all supported handles. Use the announced fixed size or the next variable size for each slice. Parse each slice by handle ID. All multi-byte values are big-endian.

HandleFieldParse
0x50004clan tagbyte0 = pair count, byte1 = trailing (0|1); byteCount = pairs×2 + trailing; remaining bytes UTF-8
0x00010005account idfirst four bytes u32 (nonzero); the whisper-target account, priority 1
0x0001001bsocial account idfirst four bytes u32; account fallback, priority 2
65561toon handleregion u8, program u32, realm u32, id u64
65556toon profilelabel u32, id u64 (a profile address)
65555avatartableId u16, offset u16 (ImageTableEntry)
0x50002in gamesingle byte, true when 0x01
0x10020 / 0x10010awayboolean; standing status
0x10022 / 0x10011busyboolean; standing status
0x00010003 / 0x00010009session marksset on entry, cleared on exit; presence is held while either is present, and drives leave detection

Use this standing-state precedence: offline, in-game, busy or away, and available. For busy and away, the last write has precedence. The account-ID fields supply the target for an outbound whisper.

Cach/9 Cache::GetStreamItemsRequest

Direction
client → server
Phase
protected bootstrap
Structure
generated order
Evidence
live verified

Requests items from a named cache stream. Bootstrap requests two localized XML catalogs from channel BNET: ERRS for authoritative error messages and CONF for public channel names and IDs. Distinct request tokens correlate their responses.

struct GetStreamItemsRequest {
    token: u32,
    generated_check: u23, // rolling check seeded with 7
    max_items_minus_1: u6, // requested item count: 1..=50
    stream_kind: bool, // true = description
    channel: FourCC,
    item_name: FourCC,
    locale: FourCC,
    reference_time: i32,
    direction: bool, // false = before, true = after
}

Cach/9 Cache::GetStreamItemsResponse

Direction
server → client
Phase
protected bootstrap
Structure
generated order
Evidence
live verified
struct GetStreamItemsResponse {
    items: Array<CacheStreamItem> {
        count_bits: 6,
        count_range: 0..=49,
    },
    token: u32,
    total_items: u16,
    offset: u16,
}

struct CacheStreamItem {
    _reserved: Reserved<23>,
    // align to the next byte
    content_handle: Bytes<40>,
    publication_time: i32,
}

The newest item is selected by publication time. In the 40-byte content handle, bytes 0..4 contain an ASCII usage suffix, bytes 4..8 contain the depot region, and bytes 8..40 contain the content hash. The primary URL is https://<region>-s2-depot.classic.blizzard.com/<hash>.<usage>. A sharded s2-depot-storage URL is the fallback.

The CONF XML maps public channel IDs to localized names. The ERRS XML stores localized messages as <e id="code">message</e>. Numeric errors from command responses, joins, toon creation, and profile operations should use that catalog first, with a static symbolic name only as a fallback.

S2Mp — SC2 multiplayer and groups

Slot 13 carries both the S2Map namespace and the Battle.net group subsystem. Blizzard also calls a group a “club.” The service lists and searches groups, reads group data, answers invitations, subscribes to game-group data, and reads map favorites.

Some decoders are positional. A positional decoder uses absolute bit offsets from the start of the record. The offsets include the route header. Generated order can add reserved bits beyond the metadata fields.

Chat — channels, roster, and messages

The four-bit service slot selects the Chat service. The three-bit channelIndex selects a joined channel. A successful join returns this index. The client must store it for messages, roster updates, and leave records. The documented implementation permits six concurrent joined channels.

bootstrap order Chat/21Chat/22 Chat/23Chat/24 Chat/25Chat/26 Chat/0Chat/1 Chat/2Chat/11 send Chat/11 receiveChat/27 Chat/19 sendChat/19 receive Chat/30Chat/20 Chat/4Chat/5 and Chat/6 Chat/9Chat/10 Chat/13 Chat/32 and Chat/33

Chat readiness

Base97563 prepares chat by selecting a playable identity and loading the regional channel directory.

  1. Request Cach/9 stream items BNET/ERRS/enUS and BNET/CONF/enUS with distinct request tokens.
  2. When Toon/0 supplies the account's playable identities, choose one with Toon/5. Wait for Toon/6.
  3. After Toon/6, send Pres/2. Then send Chat/25 and Chat/21. Collect Chat/26 pages until isLast is true, and wait for Chat/22.
  4. For a public channel, also wait for the cache response. Select the channel ID from the downloaded BNET/CONF/enUS catalog.
  5. Send Chat/0 for the desired public, private, or club channel. A successful Chat/27 assigns the channelIndex and local member handle.
  6. Apply Chat/1 membership batches until endOfInitial is true. The roster is then complete and the client can use the assigned channel index with Chat/11 and Chat/2.

These steps define state dependencies. Other protected records can occur between them, and the client must dispatch each complete record.

Choice value 1 is reserved. Generated code writes the locator before the request token. The private arm uses a seven-bit UTF-8 byte count. It then aligns to a byte and writes the name.

The club arm writes 16 zero bits before the group ID. For live group 535241, the ID starts at bit 29. The request token starts at bit 61. Live data confirms public ID 1033 and a named private room.

Appendix

Open questions

  1. Frnd/33 is defined for an empty page. The generated order for a non-empty toon-block entry is unknown.
  2. The server echo of client Chat/11 requires verification. Automated validation treats chat as read-only.
  3. Chat/20 WhisperUndeliverable has a declared command constant. Its inbound type mapping, payload, and boundary remain unresolved.
  4. Prty/0 and slot 13 command 50 use observed fixed-size skips. Their payload structures remain unresolved.
  5. Toon/23 decodes in reflection order for the current capture. Its marked layout remains a candidate pending independent confirmation.
  6. Auth/16 has the captured GenerateWebToken shape. Related generated interfaces also call the same shape GenerateAppToken, so the route's preferred semantic name remains ambiguous.
  7. Conference::CategoryDescription contains generated state and a generated locator variant outside the simple field-permutation layout model. The logical ID, name ID, and sort order are decoded; the generated internals are intentionally reported as ignored.

Glossary

Battle.net platform
The complete modern account and game-service system. It includes web authentication, Front, GameUtilities, Sunken, and game-native services.
Front WebSocket
The RFC 6455 transport with subprotocol v1.rpc.battle.net. One binary message contains one complete Front RPC message.
Cached web credential
An opaque value from AuthenticationServer method 8. A later LogonRequest can use this value. The web challenge returns a separate short-lived credential.
Front
The regional SC2 account and session connection. It carries protobuf RPC over WebSocket and supplies the native handoff.
Sunken
The SC2-native endpoint that accepts Resume authentication and then carries protected, bit-packed service records.
GameUtilities
A protobuf service available through Front. Its ProcessClientRequest method performs the SC2-specific Front-to-Sunken handoff on this path.
Protobuf descriptor
Schema metadata for a Front message or service. Service names and methods are recoverable from standard protobuf descriptors embedded in the client.
BSN metadata
Version-7 schema metadata embedded in the SC2 executable. A numeric type ID selects a structural record and an optional naming record. Front uses separate protobuf descriptors.
Frame
The explicitly named Sunken Connection/13 MessageFrame type. Front RPC messages and Sunken stream records use their own boundary terms.
Packet
An informal term that may refer to a Front RPC message, Sunken record, or TCP segment. Each term identifies a different boundary.
Record
One Sunken stream unit. A service record contains an 11-bit route, a schema-delimited payload, and final padding. A command response contains a seven-bit prefix and a nine-bit result.
Schema-delimited
A service-record boundary that the payload schema sets. Local counts, selectors, and presence bits set nested sizes. The end of the top-level value is the logical record end.
Route
The native wire tuple (direction, slot, command). Direction matters because one command number can name different request and notify types. A static build table supplies the readable service label.
Service hash
A 32-bit FNV-1a hash of a full protobuf service name. It is included in every Front request, including the initial Connect.
Front RPC token
A protobuf-header value that identifies a related RPC call. Chat requests use a separate application-level m_token.
Authentication module ID
The 40-byte ID in an Auth/2 ModuleInput. It contains an eight-byte usage prefix and a 32-byte module identity. The ID selects the module operation. Output cardinality depends on the selected modules. See the layout and known IDs.
Service slot
A four-bit number selecting a Sunken service. Slot constants are build-specific. FourCC values and chat-channel indexes occupy separate fields.
Client channel index
A three-bit Chat field that selects a local chat channel. Its wire range is 0 through 6. The service grants a maximum of six concurrent channels. A client must use a maximum of six channels. The routing header carries the service slot separately.
Front account entity ID
A 128-bit protobuf entity identifying the Battle.net platform account. It maps to a separate 32-bit account ID in native social services.
Front game-account entity ID
A 128-bit protobuf entity identifying one game account or license under a Battle.net account. The selected SC2 game account is passed to Game Utilities.
Toon handle
A stable native SC2 character identifier containing region, program, realm, and a 64-bit toon ID. Profile storage uses a separate record address.
Presence ID
A connection-local native identifier for an online presence record. Local and master IDs can be aliases. Durable identity comes from the native account ID or toon handle.
Member handle
A channel-local Chat roster key. The same person can have a different member handle in every joined channel.
LocatorKey
A native Chat choice identifying a private, public, or club conference. Public channels use a locale FourCC and a channel-name string ID.
Generated order
The field order from the generated native serializer. It can differ from metadata order and contain filler bits. A separate declarative layout can describe field permutation and filler runs.
Obfuscation marker
Bit 6 in a metadata structural record. It indicates that generated handling may apply. A separate layout supplies field order and filler widths. Some marked types use ordinary reflection order.
Resume
The native Auth exchange that continues Front authorization on Sunken. It uses Authentication::ResumeRequest and Authentication::ResumeResponse. Sunken uses a new TCP connection and fresh native chat and game state.
NO_RESPONSE
A protobuf RPC declaration requiring omission of the reply frame.
FourCC
A four-byte symbolic identifier such as Chat, Auth, Mc64, or enUS.

2026-08-16 — generated layouts and route audit
  • Documented 0x40 generated-handling eligibility and the separate wire-layout data.
  • Documented the declarative field-permutation and filler-run model, verified reflected layouts, candidate layouts, and remaining custom codecs.

  • Added Achv/0 and Achv/2, plus newly captured Auth, Conn, Chat, Party, S2Master, S2Map, Profile, and Toon routes.
  • Documented the BNET/ERRS/enUS cache catalog and depot content handle format.
